Route planning on a punctual stretch
This part of the manual describes what is expected

Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: to give clear, steady support for companion animal travel and keep each booking aligned with animal welfare needs and airline service limits.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk must greet every passenger with calm attention, gather the travel details that affect the animal, and confirm that the booking record reflects the chosen route, carrier needs, and any service notes. Staff should speak plainly, avoid pressure, and explain the next step in a way that helps the passenger feel prepared. When a welfare concern is raised, the case must be passed to the welfare coordinator for review before the trip is confirmed. If the animal has known comfort needs, the desk should note them carefully and share only the information needed for safe handling.

Service changes must be recorded in the desk ledger as soon as they are agreed, so the record stays current for the cabin team and the ground team. Staff should check that travel documents are complete, that crate or carrier details are suitable for the animal, and that any special support has been reflected in the file. If a passenger changes a request, the desk should update the file without delay and confirm the revised arrangement in simple terms. When more than one traveler is linked to the same animal booking, each note should remain clear and consistent.

During the journey, the cabin team monitors the animal in flight, while the desk remains ready to answer follow-up concerns and guide later service changes. The desk should keep a reassuring tone at all times, especially when a traveler is worried about the animal's comfort or movement through the airport. If a case becomes unclear, staff should pause, verify the record, and seek guidance rather than guess. Contact the senior service lead for unresolved cases, exceptions, or any concern that cannot be settled through normal desk process.
